editorialNote: Focused KB for Leber Congenital Amaurosis. LCA is a genetic early-onset severe retinal dystrophy with ~25 causative genes. Gene-specific therapies dominate: (1) voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna, FDA 2017) for biallelic RPE65 LCA/IRD — first FDA-approved gene therapy for an inherited disease; (2) EDIT-101 (brilliant, Editas) — first-ever in-vivo CRISPR clinical trial, for CEP290 p.Cys998X (LCA10); Editas discontinued late 2022 and transitioned trial assets to Eyedocs/academic hands. (3) Sepofarsen (QR-110, ProQR) antisense oligonucleotide for same CEP290 LCA10 splice-site variant — phase 2/3 ILLUMINATE FAILED 2022, program halted. Any LCA output that fails to mention Luxturna for RPE65 or discuss the CEP290 therapeutic history (BRILLIANCE paused + sepofarsen failed) is AI slop.

commonComorbidities: Keratoconus (frequent in LCA patients, related to eye rubbing / oculo-digital sign)
Photophobia or night blindness (varies by genotype — e.g., RPE65 LCA features profound early night blindness)
Developmental and psychosocial impact of early vision loss
lifestyleCategories: Genetic testing (single best first step) — My Retina Tracker (FFB) or commercial IRD panel
Pediatric ophthalmology + low-vision rehab referral at diagnosis
Educational services (Braille, orientation + mobility training, assistive tech)
Avoid eye rubbing where possible (keratoconus prevention)
School-based Individualized Education Program (IEP) for visual impairment
Screen for cataracts annually from adolescence

items.title: Efficacy and safety of voretigene neparvovec (AAV2-hRPE65v2) in patients with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal dystrophy: a randomised, controlled, open-label, phase 3 trial
items.authors: Russell S, Bennett J, Wellman JA, et al.
items.summary: Pivotal phase 3 RCT of voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna) in 31 patients with biallelic RPE65-mutation retinal dystrophy. Primary endpoint (multi-luminance mobility test change at year 1) significantly improved in treated vs control. Basis for FDA approval December 2017 — the FIRST FDA-approved gene therapy for an inherited disease. Technique: subretinal injection under general anesthesia by specialized vitreoretinal surgeon.

keyPassages.quote: At 1 year, the mean bilateral MLMT change score was 1.8 (SD 1.1) light levels in the intervention group versus 0.2 (SD 1.0) in the control group (difference 1.6, 95% CI 0.72-2.41; P=0.0013).

items.title: LUXTURNA (voretigene neparvovec-rzyl) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: First FDA-approved gene therapy for an inherited disease. Indication: biallelic RPE65 mutation-associated retinal dystrophy. AAV2-hRPE65v2 delivered via subretinal injection under general anesthesia in each eye, separated by 6-18 days. Covers only the ~0.3-1% of IRD patients with biallelic RPE65 mutations. List price ~$850,000 for both eyes.

keyPassages.quote: LUXTURNA is indicated for the treatment of patients with confirmed biallelic RPE65 mutation-associated retinal dystrophy.

items.title: Development of a gene-editing approach to restore vision loss in Leber congenital amaurosis type 10 (preclinical)
items.authors: Maeder ML, Stefanidakis M, Wilson CJ, et al.
items.summary: Preclinical foundation paper for EDIT-101 (AGN-151587): CRISPR-Cas9 in-vivo excision of the CEP290 intronic IVS26 c.2991+1655A>G variant that creates a cryptic splice site in ~15-20% of LCA10 patients. Led to BRILLIANCE first in-vivo CRISPR human trial.

items.title: Editas Medicine discontinues commercial development of EDIT-101 (BRILLIANCE) for LCA10
items.summary: November 2022 — Editas Medicine announced it would not pursue commercial development of EDIT-101 for LCA10, after a portfolio reprioritization toward hematology (EDIT-301 for sickle cell). Trial assets transitioned to academic partners. This is a consequential inflection point for CEP290 LCA10 therapeutic options. Sepofarsen (ProQR) also failed earlier in 2022 — leaving CEP290 LCA10 without a late-stage therapeutic option.

items.title: ProQR discontinues sepofarsen (QR-110) phase 2/3 ILLUMINATE for LCA10 after trial fails primary endpoint
items.summary: February 2022 — ProQR reported that the phase 2/3 ILLUMINATE trial of sepofarsen (QR-110) — an intravitreal antisense oligonucleotide restoring CEP290 mRNA splicing in patients with the c.2991+1655A>G variant — did NOT meet its primary endpoint (BCVA change at 12 months). ProQR halted development and ultimately reprioritized its pipeline (acquired by Laboratoires Théa 2024 for axiomabtagene cost-effective pathway).

canonicalFacts.claim: Voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna) is the first FDA-approved gene therapy for an inherited disease (December 2017), for biallelic RPE65 mutation-associated retinal dystrophy — a small subset (~0.3-1%) of IRD patients.
Sepofarsen (ProQR QR-110 antisense) for CEP290 c.2991+1655A>G LCA10 FAILED the phase 2/3 ILLUMINATE trial February 2022; ProQR discontinued the program.
EDIT-101 (Editas BRILLIANCE CRISPR) for CEP290 LCA10 was the first in-vivo CRISPR human trial; Editas discontinued commercial development November 2022 as part of strategic reprioritization.

redFlags: Physicians generally caution against considering Luxturna without confirmed BIALLELIC RPE65 mutations on accredited genetic testing.
Literature does not support offering sepofarsen as a treatment option — the ILLUMINATE phase 2/3 failed in 2022 and the program is discontinued.

Literature warns against seeking unapproved stem-cell or gene-therapy treatments from clinics in China, India, Mexico, Panama, or elsewhere — multiple FDA warning letters, no peer-reviewed efficacy data for LCA, high infection and complication risk.
Physicians generally caution against delaying genetic testing — it is the single action that opens or closes every therapeutic and trial option.

Avoid self-pay 'gene therapy' or 'peptide therapy' programs that are not on ClinicalTrials.gov — legitimate programs are FDA-regulated and legitimate programs typically do not charge patients for investigational products.

pipelineDrugs.name: Voretigene neparvovec
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: AAV2 gene replacement delivering RPE65 cDNA by subretinal injection
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved December 2017 for biallelic RPE65 mutation IRD including LCA2
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First FDA-approved gene therapy for an inherited disease. Any LCA output must address Luxturna for RPE65 patients.

pipelineDrugs.name: EDIT-101 (brilliant)
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: In-vivo subretinal CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing to excise CEP290 IVS26 c.2991+1655A>G cryptic splice-site variant
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 1/2 BRILLIANCE ongoing at reduced commercial priority; Editas DISCONTINUED commercial development November 2022
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First in-vivo CRISPR human trial. Historically significant but commercial path unclear. Patients asking about 'CRISPR for LCA' need accurate framing.

pipelineDrugs.name: Sepofarsen
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Intravitreal antisense oligonucleotide restoring normal CEP290 mRNA splicing in c.2991+1655A>G carriers
pipelineDrugs.status: ILLUMINATE phase 2/3 FAILED primary endpoint February 2022; program DISCONTINUED
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Notable failed program. Must be addressed as discontinued for families still asking.

pipelineDrugs.name: jCell (human retinal progenitor cells)
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Intravitreal injection of allogeneic human retinal progenitor cells (neurotrophic paracrine hypothesis)
pipelineDrugs.status: Primarily in retinitis pigmentosa phase 2b/3 (NCT03073733); not specifically for LCA
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Gene-agnostic cell therapy; may be relevant to LCA patients with residual photoreceptor function.

pipelineDrugs.name: OCU400 (Ocugen modifier gene therapy)
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Gene-agnostic AAV delivery of NR2E3 nuclear hormone receptor as master regulator
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 3 liMeliGhT for retinitis pigmentosa; LCA subtype activity under investigation
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Gene-agnostic approach — if successful in RP, likely expands to LCA subsets. Patients ask about it.

pipelineDrugs.name: RST-001 (optogenetic channelrhodopsin) / MCO-010
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Optogenetic gene therapy — converting remaining retinal bipolar or ganglion cells into photoreceptors
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 2b RESTORE completed for retinitis pigmentosa (2024 readout); LCA extension under consideration
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Gene-agnostic vision restoration for advanced IRD. May eventually apply to LCA with severe vision loss.

pipelineDrugs.name: N-acetylcysteine (oral NAC)
pipelineDrugs.sponsor: Generic / academic (Johns Hopkins NAC Attack study)
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 3 NAC Attack in retinitis pigmentosa ongoing; LCA subset not specifically targeted
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Cheap repurposing candidate under active study; gene-agnostic.

excludedAgents.name: Sepofarsen (QR-110)
excludedAgents.reason: ILLUMINATE phase 2/3 failed primary endpoint February 2022; ProQR discontinued the program. Not a treatment option.

excludedAgents.name: EDIT-101 (commercial pathway)
excludedAgents.reason: Editas Medicine discontinued commercial development November 2022. Trial assets transitioned but no commercial product is anticipated.
